title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: launch a Data Security Investigation from a case
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap dates, documented controls, permissions and consumption billing are supported. The purge description should include the supported data sources and retention qualifications, and two checklist instructions name controls absent from the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let administrators launch a pre-scoped Data Security Investigation from an Insider Risk Management case.
claims.quote: Launch a pre-scoped Data Security Investigation (DSI) from an IRM case.

claims.claim: The planned investigation lets a data security administrator view content analysis related to a risky user and assess post-incident data impact.
claims.quote: allowing them to view content analysis related to that user and better assess post-incident data impact.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Data Security Investigations uses consumption billing for storage and AI compute.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Data Security Investigations does not require a dedicated enterprise plan or licence.
claims.quote: However, you don't need a dedicated enterprise plan or license to use Data Security Investigations.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The pages reviewed do not publish government-cloud-specific storage or compute rates.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations GCC GCC High DoD government cloud billing pricing availability; opened DSI billing, GCC deployments and azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview/. No government-specific numeric DSI rates appeared in the returned text.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the government-cloud integration's default behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations default Insider; Data Security Investigations Insider Risk case pseudonymization default enable disable integration. Read roadmap, DSI overview, investigation, get-started and billing; none states this rollout's default.

claims.claim: IRM role-group membership is edited at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane. Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a management role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: DSI administrator membership is edited at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > Data Security Investigations Admins > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Role groups in the left navigation. Select the Data Security Investigations Admins role group, then select Edit. Select Choose users

claims.claim: The generic Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" call adds role-group membership and its effective permissions.
claims.quote: When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: AI capacity setup is at Microsoft Purview portal > Data Security Investigations > Setup tasks > Set up AI capacity.
claims.quote: Go to Data Security Investigations in the Microsoft Purview portal and sign in with the credentials for a user account assigned Data Security Investigations permissions. Select Set up AI capacity in the Setup tasks section.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an automation operation for DSI AI capacity setup.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations AI capacity PowerShell API configuration; Data Security Investigations PowerShell capacity; Data Security Investigations Graph capacity. Read DSI billing and get-started; no setup cmdlet or endpoint was returned.

claims.claim: Per-investigation consumption is viewed at Microsoft Purview portal > Data Security Investigations > Usage dashboard.
claims.quote: Go to Data Security Investigations in the Microsoft Purview portal and sign in with the credentials for a user account assigned to the Data Security Investigations Administrator role group. Select Usage dashboard in the left-navigation.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a DSI usage-dashboard API or PowerShell operation.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations usage API PowerShell dashboard. Read DSI billing, including Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard and Export; results gave the portal dashboard and export, not a DSI consumption API or cmdlet.

claims.claim: Audit searches are configured at Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is the PowerShell command for searching the unified audit log.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember is a general Exchange and Security & Compliance role-group cmdlet whose reference does not name DSI groups.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. Applicable: Exchange Server 2010, Exchange Server 2013, Exchange Server 2016, Exchange Server 2019, Exchange Server SE, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Who can launch; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Creating an investigation from an IRM case requires at least one of the Insider Risk Management or Insider Risk Management Investigator roles.
claims.quote: To create investigations in Data Security Investigations in Insider Risk Management, you must have at least one of the following roles assigned: Insider Risk Management; Insider Risk Management Investigator

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management role group automatically includes Data Security Investigation Contributor access.
claims.quote: the following Microsoft Purview role groups automatically include Data Security Investigations roles. Insider Risk Management | Data Security Investigation Contributor | Contributor access

claims.claim: Data Security Investigation Contributors can create and manage investigations they own or belong to.
claims.quote: Members with the Data Security Investigation Contributor role can create and manage investigations they own or are members of.

claims.claim: The Contributor role does not include access to data storage.
claims.quote: This role doesn't include access to data storage, AI job execution, or the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard.

claims.claim: The Contributor role does not include AI job execution.
claims.quote: This role doesn't include access to data storage, AI job execution, or the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard.

claims.claim: The Contributor role does not include usage-dashboard access.
claims.quote: This role doesn't include access to data storage, AI job execution, or the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard.

claims.claim: Global Administrators need DSI role-group permissions to create and access investigations.
claims.quote: Global admins must be assigned to one of the listed role groups for Data Security Investigations to create and access investigations.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Compliance Administrator role-group members inherit the DSI Admin role.
claims.quote: Compliance Administrator | Data Security Investigation Admin | Full administrative access

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Organization Management role-group members inherit DSI administrative access.
claims.quote: Organization Management | Data Security Investigation Admin, Data Security Investigation Contributor | Administrative and contributor access

claims.claim: Configuring AI capacity requires membership of the Data Security Investigations Admins role group.
claims.quote: To configure the AI capacity for Data Security Investigations, you must be a member of the Data Security Investigations Admins role group.

claims.claim: Viewing the usage dashboard requires the Data Security Investigations Admin role.
claims.quote: Only users assigned the Data Security Investigations Admin role can access the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard.

claims.claim: The latest usage-dashboard billing data can take up to 48 hours to appear.
claims.quote: It might take up to 48 hours for the latest billing data to show up on the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard for your organization.

claims.claim: Portal audit searches require Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Audit cmdlets require Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Exchange admin center.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog must run in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Data Security Investigations activities are automatically logged in the unified audit log.
claims.quote: To meet these requirements, Data Security Investigations activities are automatically logged in the unified audit log.

claims.claim: A case-based launch follows Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Cases > case > Case actions > Investigate data security with AI.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Insider Risk Management > Cases and select a case. On the Cases page, select Case actions. Select Investigate data security with AI.

claims.claim: The case-launch dialog asks for an investigation name.
claims.quote: In the Name field, enter a name for the investigation (required).

claims.claim: The case-launch dialog offers an optional description.
claims.quote: In the Description field, add an optional description to help others understand this investigation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Investigation scope field lets the investigator choose which case items to include.
claims.quote: In the Investigation scope field, choose the items from the case to include in the investigation.

claims.claim: The dialog offers an Additional context for AI field.
claims.quote: In the Additional context for AI field, enter additional context to help AI focus your investigation on specific areas and issues.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Case items are automatically included as data sources of the new investigation.
claims.quote: The items included in the case are automatically included as data sources.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Adding shared items to the investigation scope starts processing automatically.
claims.quote: If you add the shared items to the scope of the investigation, processing automatically starts so you can dig further into the details of the content.

claims.claim: Investigators can review preliminary insights about the shared content.
claims.quote: With built-in integration, you can create a new investigation in Data Security Investigations from the Insider Risk Management case to quickly review preliminary insights about the shared content.

claims.claim: Investigators can decide whether further content analysis is needed before committing additional compute resources or charges.
claims.quote: Before committing any additional compute resources or charges, you can decide if this content needs further analysis.

claims.where: What's changing: third paragraph; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Investigations created from IRM cases containing more than approximately 3,000 items might return incomplete results.
claims.quote: Investigations created from Insider Risk Management cases that contain more than approximately 3,000 items might not return complete results. The exact limit depends on the file names and paths of the returned items.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The reviewed DSI Learn pages do not identify their supported clouds or confirm government-cloud AI and billing availability.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations GCC; Data Security Investigations government; Data Security Investigations GCC GCC High DoD government cloud billing pricing availability. Read DSI overview, investigation, billing, permissions and get-started; no cloud-specific support statement.

claims.claim: The GCC deployments planning page has no Data Security Investigations entry in its feature table.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations GCC. Opened and read the complete feature table in Plan for Microsoft Purview compliance and risk management solutions - GCC deployments; it contains no Data Security Investigations row.

claims.claim: Microsoft says IRM investigators might lack important insights into file content associated with risky alerts.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management investigators might not have important insights into the content contained in files associated with risky alerts.

claims.claim: Analysts use AI categorisation, vector search and examination for investigation analysis.
claims.quote: There are three main AI-related investigative capabilities: Vector search; Categorization; Examination. Analysts query impacted data to find all assets related to a particular subject, even if keywords are missing.

claims.claim: DSI supports soft purge to remove items from data sources.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations supports soft purge and hard purge options to remove or permanently delete items from data sources.
claims.fix: Narrow the purge sentence to 'Data Security Investigations supports soft purge for Exchange mailbox items and hard purge for Exchange mailbox items and Teams messages.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations-mitigation-actions, whose supported-data-sources table gives these qualifications.

claims.claim: DSI supports hard purge to permanently delete items from data sources.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations supports soft purge and hard purge options to remove or permanently delete items from data sources.
claims.fix: Add 'Both purge methods respect holds and retention policies; items subject to them cannot be permanently deleted until the hold is removed or the retention period expires.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations-mitigation-actions, which states this qualification.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Both billing models must be configured before using DSI.
claims.quote: Before you can use Data Security Investigations in your organization, you must configure both billing models.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Billing setup requires an Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: To configure the storage meter and capacity for Data Security Investigations, you must have: An Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Billing setup requires a resource group in that Azure subscription.
claims.quote: An Azure resource group in that subscription.

claims.claim: Storage-meter billing setup requires the Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: To configure the storage meter and capacity for Data Security Investigations, you must have: The Global Administrator role.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Billing setup requires the resource group's Owner or Contributor role.
claims.quote: The resource group Owner or Contributor role.

claims.claim: Stopping DSI billing deletes all investigations.
claims.quote: To stop billing for Data Security Investigations, disable both storage meter and AI capacity support. This action deletes all investigations in Data Security Investigations and deletes compute units for your resource group.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The storage meter is pay-as-you-go per gigabyte per month across all investigations in the organisation.
claims.quote: The storage meter for Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model. You pay for storage on a gigabyte (GB) per month basis for stored data associated with all investigations in your organization.

claims.claim: Storage charges are prorated by the number of days data was stored.
claims.quote: The charges are prorated to the number of days the data was stored in the billing cycle.

claims.claim: Creating an investigation, using storage and deleting it within a single 24-hour period still incurs a storage charge.
claims.quote: If you create an investigation, use data storage, and then delete the investigation in a single 24-hour period, you pay for the storage amount.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: AI analysis consumes pay-as-you-go compute units.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model for AI capacity. You need compute units for deep analysis and AI-related processing in your investigations. You pay only for the compute units you use.

claims.claim: Failed compute-unit operations are not billed.
claims.quote: You aren't billed for failed compute unit operations but are billed for partial completions.

claims.claim: Partially completed compute-unit operations are billed.
claims.quote: You aren't billed for failed compute unit operations but are billed for partial completions.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meters; Why it matters
claims.claim: DSI charges flow through the Azure subscription and resource group associated during setup.
claims.quote: Storage meter billing requires a link to an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing. Resource group: The resource group in your Azure subscription you want to assign to the storage meter. AI analysis is billed through compute units in Microsoft Azure.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls on spend
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends using the in-product cost estimator before starting investigations.
claims.quote: Use the in-product cost estimator before starting investigations: Before launching an investigation, use the in-product cost estimator to anticipate costs based on investigation size and the analyses you plan to conduct.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls on spend; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Azure budgets at the DSI resource-group and meter levels.
claims.quote: Create budgets for the Data Security Investigations resource group and meter level.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls on spend; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends alerts when spending approaches defined thresholds.
claims.quote: Configure alerts when spending approaches defined thresholds (for example, 50%, 75%, or 90%).

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls on spend
claims.claim: The DSI billing page does not state that budgets or alerts stop use at a threshold.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations budgets threshold stop cap. Read the complete DSI billing page and returned cost-management excerpts; they describe budgets and approaching-threshold alerts, not an automatic usage stop.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Controls on spend
claims.claim: Deleting an investigation stops its associated storage charge, subject to the stated daily prorating.
claims.quote: When you delete an investigation, you stop paying for the associated data storage amount. The charges are prorated to the number of days the data was stored in the billing cycle.

claims.claim: AI capacity setup includes choosing the AI analysis data processing location.
claims.quote: AI analysis data processing location: The primary country/region. Select from the available locations.

claims.claim: Keeping at least one user in the DSI Admins role group avoids a zero-administrator configuration.
claims.quote: Always have at least one user in the Data Security Investigations Admins role group so that your Data Security Investigations configuration doesn't get in to a 'zero administrator' scenario if specific users leave your organization.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's storage-meter configuration instruction has no matching control row.
claims.quote: Checklist: Configure the storage meter and AI capacity, choosing the AI analysis data processing location. Table: AI capacity set-up for Data Security Investigations; no storage-meter setup row.
claims.fix: The 'Configure the storage meter' part of the At rollout checklist has no row. Narrow that bullet to 'Configure AI capacity, choosing the AI analysis data processing location.' Do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to keep investigation scope narrow has no investigation-scope control row.
claims.quote: Checklist: Brief investigators to keep the investigation scope narrow and to stay below roughly 3,000 items per case-based investigation. Table covers role membership, AI capacity, usage dashboard and audit, not investigation scope.
claims.fix: The 'keep the investigation scope narrow' checklist instruction has no row. Narrow that bullet to 'Brief investigators that investigations created from IRM cases containing more than approximately 3,000 items might return incomplete results.' Leave the existing scope advice in Risk assessment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap says IRM users are pseudonymised by default.
claims.quote: Built with privacy by design, users are pseudonymized by default, and role-based access controls and audit logs are in place to help ensure user-level privacy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The reviewed documentation does not say whether IRM pseudonymisation carries into the investigation created from a case.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations pseudonym; Data Security Investigations Insider Risk case pseudonymization default enable disable integration. Read DSI overview, investigation and permissions; privacy search excerpts discuss IRM, not pseudonym transfer into DSI.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published
claims.claim: The DSI billing page links to Azure's Purview pricing page for storage rates.
claims.quote: For more data storage rates and pricing, see Data Security Investigations storage meter pricing.
